chainNotes.title: Robinhood Chain publishes no L2 sequencer-uptime feed, yet its docs require checking one
chainNotes.statement: Robinhood's oracle documentation instructs callers to "verify the sequencer is up before trusting a price" because during a sequencer outage feeds can go stale. No such feed could be found: the Robinhood Chain Chainlink reference-data directory contains 57 feeds and none is a sequencer-uptime feed, and chain 4663 does not appear on Chainlink's L2 Sequencer Uptime Feeds page, which lists Arbitrum, Base, Celo, Mantle, MegaETH, Metis, OP, Scroll, Soneium, X Layer and ZKsync. The recommended control therefore cannot be performed on this chain today. Stated as "not found in the published directories" rather than "does not exist".

chainNotes.title: 160 of 195 scanned Stock Tokens have no Chainlink price feed
chainNotes.statement: The Robinhood Chain Chainlink reference-data directory publishes 57 feeds, of which 35 are 24/5 equity feeds. 160 of the 195 Stock Tokens scanned have no feed entry, so they cannot be priced on-chain at all and any valuation must come from an off-chain source — which reintroduces the cross-surface mixing hazard. 21 of them also carry a uiMultiplier() other than 1.0, where an off-chain SHARE price differs from token value by that multiplier: CRM (1.0011x), CRWD (4.0000x), AVGO (1.0013x), CCL (1.0215x), PR (1.0045x), and 16 more.

findings.subject: CRM (0xd95B44124e475743a7589e68F3D74008A5536D44)
findings.affectedParty: Any integrator that presents CRM balanceOf() as a share count. The contract itself is behaving as ERC-8056 specifies and is not at fault.
findings.title: CRM: reading balanceOf() as shares understates by 0.1147% (multiplier 1.001148323x)
findings.statement: CRM reports uiMultiplier() = 1001148322800714293 (1.001148323), which is CORRECT AND SPEC-COMPLIANT behaviour under ERC-8056 — this finding is not a defect in the token contract. It records the exposure carried by a caller that reads balanceOf() as shares. Under ERC-8056 a corporate action moves the multiplier rather than balances, so balanceOf() returns tokens and share-equivalents = balance * uiMultiplier() / 1e18. A surface presenting the raw balance as a share count understates it by 0.1147% (the true count is 1.0011x the raw balance). Token value computed as balance * Chainlink feed price is unaffected, because the feed is already multiplier-adjusted.

impact.note: totalSupply raw 302.6430 tokens vs 302.9905 share-equivalents (delta 0.3475). Presenting the raw balance as a share count understates by 0.1147%; equivalently the true count is 1.0011x the raw.

findings.subject: SPY (0x117cc2133c37B721F49dE2A7a74833232B3B4C0C)
findings.affectedParty: Any caller that values SPY with an off-chain SHARE price, or computes a premium/discount between the on-chain token price and an off-chain share price.
findings.title: SPY: off-chain share price and on-chain token price differ by 0.172%
findings.statement: The Chainlink feed returns a multiplier-adjusted TOKEN price (773.0897), while Robinhood's REST /prices endpoint returns the RAW UNDERLYING share price (mid 774.1200). These are different quantities related by uiMultiplier(): underlying x 1.001717991 = 775.4499, leaving a residual of -0.304% against the observed feed price. That residual is NOT small relative to the 0.172% multiplier effect, so it is reported as an observation and no cause is asserted for it. Bid/ask spread and quote timing are plausible contributors but are not established here; a trading halt on the underlying would also produce it, and this sweep does not test that. The finding stands on the multiplier relationship itself, which is byte-verified: valuing balanceOf() with an off-chain share price, or computing a premium/discount between an on-chain token price and an off-chain share price, produces a phantom error of 0.172%.

impact.note: feed 773.0897 vs underlying-mid 774.1200 x multiplier 1.001717991 = 775.4499

offChainSources.describes: underlying share bid/ask used for the mid 774.1200 (not multiplier-adjusted)

findings.statement: SGOV reports uiMultiplier() = 1005101770003214918 (1.005101770), which is CORRECT AND SPEC-COMPLIANT behaviour under ERC-8056 — this finding is not a defect in the token contract. It records the exposure carried by a caller that reads balanceOf() as shares. Under ERC-8056 a corporate action moves the multiplier rather than balances, so balanceOf() returns tokens and share-equivalents = balance * uiMultiplier() / 1e18. A surface presenting the raw balance as a share count understates it by 0.5076% (the true count is 1.0051x the raw balance). Token value computed as balance * Chainlink feed price is unaffected, because the feed is already multiplier-adjusted.

impact.note: totalSupply raw 36836.3122 tokens vs 37024.2426 share-equivalents (delta 187.9304). Presenting the raw balance as a share count understates by 0.5076%; equivalently the true count is 1.0051x the raw.

findings.subject: SGOV (0x92FD66527192E3e61d4DDd13322Aa222DE86F9B5)
findings.affectedParty: Any caller that values SGOV with an off-chain SHARE price, or computes a premium/discount between the on-chain token price and an off-chain share price.
findings.title: SGOV: off-chain share price and on-chain token price differ by 0.510%
findings.statement: The Chainlink feed returns a multiplier-adjusted TOKEN price (101.1082), while Robinhood's REST /prices endpoint returns the RAW UNDERLYING share price (mid 100.6050). These are different quantities related by uiMultiplier(): underlying x 1.005101770 = 101.1183, leaving a residual of -0.010% against the observed feed price. That residual is small relative to the 0.510% multiplier effect, consistent with bid/ask spread and the timing gap between the REST quote and the feed's updatedAt. The finding stands on the multiplier relationship itself, which is byte-verified: valuing balanceOf() with an off-chain share price, or computing a premium/discount between an on-chain token price and an off-chain share price, produces a phantom error of 0.510%.

A surface presenting the raw balance as a share count understates it by 0.0101% (the true count is 1.0001x the raw balance). Token value computed as balance * Chainlink feed price is unaffected, because the feed is already multiplier-adjusted.

findings.subject: ASML (0x47F93d52cBeC7C6D2CfC080e154002370a60dAEA)
findings.affectedParty: Any caller that values ASML with an off-chain SHARE price, or computes a premium/discount between the on-chain token price and an off-chain share price.
findings.title: ASML: off-chain share price and on-chain token price differ by 0.010%
findings.statement: The Chainlink feed returns a multiplier-adjusted TOKEN price (1721.7594), while Robinhood's REST /prices endpoint returns the RAW UNDERLYING share price (mid 1722.9250). These are different quantities related by uiMultiplier(): underlying x 1.000101323 = 1723.0996, leaving a residual of -0.078% against the observed feed price. That residual is NOT small relative to the 0.010% multiplier effect, so it is reported as an observation and no cause is asserted for it. Bid/ask spread and quote timing are plausible contributors but are not established here; a trading halt on the underlying would also produce it, and this sweep does not test that. The finding stands on the multiplier relationship itself, which is byte-verified: valuing balanceOf() with an off-chain share price, or computing a premium/discount between an on-chain token price and an off-chain share price, produces a phantom error of 0.010%.
